claims.text: Adaptive sampling will improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
Metadynamics will improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
Improved representation of liquid atomic configurations will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap.
The proposed sampling methods will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 25% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Adaptive sampling adjusts sampling parameters on the fly.
On-the-fly adjustment in adaptive sampling optimizes exploration of phase space.
The metadynamics bias drives the system toward previously unexplored regions of phase space.
More efficient and systematic exploration of the potential-energy landscape improves representation of liquid configurations.
The intervention is applicable to both solid and liquid states at and near high melting temperatures.
The applicable temperature range is 0.8 to 1.2 times the alloy melting temperature.
The applicable materials are near-equimolar multicomponent high-entropy alloys in which each component constitutes 10–50% of the composition.
The adaptive-sampling protocol should use at least 1000 iterations and a maximum displacement of 0.1 Å.
The metadynamics protocol should use a bias factor of 10 and a deposition rate of 0.01.
The effectiveness of advanced sampling may depend on the selected parameters and the complexity of the alloy system.
Comparison with TOR-TILD's EAM references may be sensitive to the specific EAM implementation.
The hypothesis is falsified if path mismatch is reduced by less than 15% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references and that result is statistically significant at p < 0.05.
